boundary: Local interim diagnostic evidence, not a leaderboard or production claim. Retrieval numbers are the ERB doc-recall measurements from docs/ERB_EMBEDDING_EVIDENCE.md (local Gemma judge). See docs/PUBLIC_CLAIMS_POLICY.md.
selection_rule: Maximize overall_doc_recall; on a tie (within 0.5), prefer the smaller index_bytes_per_vector; the caller may still override for cost.

candidates.name: lexical-bm25-baseline
candidates.notes: Headline lexical-only ERB run; the retrieval baseline.

candidates.name: bge-m3-dense
candidates.notes: Dense+lexical hybrid over pre-embedded corpus_bge_m3.jsonl. +11.8 overall doc recall vs lexical; flat on the semantic type (a decomposition problem, not a dense-similarity one).

chosen.name: bge-m3-dense
chosen.rationale: Highest overall doc recall (67.5 vs 55.7). Multilingual (EN+RU) single dense vector fits the engine's i16 vector index; 2 KB/vector at Q15 i16. It does NOT fix the weak `semantic` pool (flat recall) — that needs query decomposition (A3/A4), not a different embedding model. Metric dot_product matches the engine default for normalized bge-m3 vectors.
